question: 10 nibbles are equal to _______ bits.
solution:
The correct answer is __**40**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 1 nibble is equal to 4 bits.
 
• Therefore, 10 nibbles will be equal to 10 * 4 = 40 bits.
 
• Nibbles are used in computing to represent four binary digits or half of an 8-bit byte.
 
• This makes it easier to manage and process data in computing systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bits:** The smallest unit of data in a computer, representing a binary value of 0 or 1.
 
• **Bytes:** A group of 8 bits, often used to encode a single character of text in a computer.
 
• **Nibbles:** A nibble is half a byte, consisting of 4 bits. It is used to represent hexadecimal digits, which range from 0 to F.
 
• **Hexadecimal System:** A base-16 numbering system used in mathematics and computing, utilizing digits 0-9 and letters A-F to represent values.
 
• **Binary System:** A base-2 numbering system used internally by almost all modern computers and computer-based devices because it is straightforward to implement with digital electronic circuitry.
